title: Depot antipsychotic injection volumes
blurb: Calculate depot antipsychotic volumes from concentrated labels, choose the right strength, and count the ampoules you need.
question: A service user is prescribed flupentixol decanoate 30 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 20 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up?

teach.body: Formal rule: volume = (dose prescribed ÷ dose in the ampoule) × ampoule volume. Plain English: depots are ordinary want ÷ have sums, but the labels are concentrated (often 100, 200 or 500 mg in 1 mL), so the volumes are small and a misread strength makes a big error. The mental health Part A paper used a flupentixol decanoate depot. Part A tests the arithmetic only, never which depot or dose to choose.
teach.cite: Pearson VUE NMC practice paper (mental health, Part A)

teach.text: Picking up the wrong strength of the same depot. Flupentixol decanoate and zuclopenthixol decanoate each come in more than one strength, so a 20 mg/mL calculation done with a 100 mg/mL ampoule gives five times the dose. In the exam, use the strength in the stem; on the ward, check it against the chart.

teach.body: Part A will not ask you to convert an oral antipsychotic dose into a depot dose, or to choose a depot interval. It gives the prescription and the label and asks for a volume, a number of ampoules or a total. Answers go in with their unit (for example 0.6 mL), with a leading zero below 1 and no trailing zero.
teach.cite: Pearson VUE NMC practice tests, answer-format guidance

items: Depot volume = dose ÷ ampoule strength × ampoule volume.
The same depot can come in two strengths: read the one in the stem.
Volumes are often small; a leading zero is required (0.6 mL).
Ampoules needed: divide, then round UP to a whole ampoule.
Part A tests the arithmetic only, never depot choice or equivalence.

summary: You can now calculate depot antipsychotic injection volumes from concentrated labels and avoid the wrong-strength error. You can also work out how many ampoules to open and totals across several doses.

A.q: A service user is prescribed flupentixol decanoate 30 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 20 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.
A.why: Want ÷ have × volume = 30 ÷ 20 × 1 = 1.5 mL. Sense-check: 30 mg is one and a half times 20 mg.

whyNot.0: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction (0.67 rounds to 0.7).
whyNot.1: This treats the label as 20 mg in 2 mL.
whyNot.3: This uses a 100 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 20 mg in 1 mL on the label.

A.q: A service user is prescribed zuclopenthixol decanoate 250 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 200 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This rounds to one decimal place; the stem asks for two.
whyNot.3: This uses a 500 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 200 mg in 1 mL on the label.

A.q: A service user is prescribed haloperidol decanoate 75 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 50 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction (0.67 rounds to 0.7).
whyNot.1: This uses a 100 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 50 mg in 1 mL on the label.
whyNot.2: This treats the label as 50 mg in 2 mL.

B.q: A service user is prescribed flupentixol decanoate 60 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 100 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction (1.67 rounds to 1.7).
whyNot.2: This uses a 20 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 100 mg in 1 mL on the label.
whyNot.3: This moves the decimal point one place, giving a tenfold error.

B.q: A service user is prescribed zuclopenthixol decanoate 350 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 500 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction (1.43 rounds to 1.4).
whyNot.1: This uses a 200 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 500 mg in 1 mL on the label.
whyNot.2: This reads the label as 50 mg in 1 mL, a tenfold error.

B.q: A service user is prescribed haloperidol decanoate 125 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoules available each contain 50 mg in 1 mL. How many ampoules need to be opened?
B.why: 125 ÷ 50 = 2.5 ampoules. You cannot open half an ampoule, so round up: 3 ampoules (2.5 mL drawn up, the rest discarded).

whyNot.0: This rounds down: two ampoules hold 100 mg, less than the 125 mg prescribed.
whyNot.1: This is the exact quotient, but a part ampoule cannot be opened.
whyNot.3: This doubles the count, as if each ampoule held 25 mg.

C.q: A service user is prescribed zuclopenthixol decanoate 600 mg, given as two equal injections at separate sites. The ampoule label reads 500 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up for each injection? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.
C.why: Each injection = 600 ÷ 2 = 300 mg. Volume = 300 ÷ 500 × 1 = 0.6 mL per injection.

whyNot.1: This is the volume for the whole dose, not each of the two injections.
whyNot.2: This is have ÷ want for one injection, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This uses a 200 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 500 mg in 1 mL on the label.

C.q: A service user is prescribed flupentixol decanoate 0.04 g by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 20 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This converts 0.04 g to 400 mg, a tenfold error.
whyNot.1: This converts 0.04 g to 4 mg, a tenfold error the other way.
whyNot.3: This uses a 100 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 20 mg in 1 mL on the label.

C.q: A service user is prescribed haloperidol decanoate 100 mg every 4 weeks. The ampoules available each contain 50 mg in 1 mL. How many ampoules are needed for the next three doses?
C.why: Each dose needs 100 ÷ 50 = 2 ampoules. Three doses need 2 × 3 = 6 ampoules.

whyNot.0: This is the number for one dose, not three.
whyNot.2: This allows one ampoule per dose; each dose needs two.
whyNot.3: This multiplies by the 4-week interval instead of the 3 doses.

reteach.title: Read the strength, then divide
reteach.question: Flupentixol decanoate 40 mg is prescribed. The ampoule says 100 mg in 1 mL. What volume?

blocks.body: 40 ÷ 100 × 1 = 0.4 mL. The answer is smaller than 1 mL because the ampoule holds more than the dose. Write the leading zero: 0.4 mL.

blocks.text: Calculating with one strength and drawing up from the other. The drug name on both boxes is the same; only the mg per mL differs.

explain.body: When the ampoule holds more than the dose, the volume is less than 1 mL. 20 mg from 100 mg in 1 mL is 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2 mL.

test.q: A service user is prescribed flupentixol decanoate 20 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 100 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.1: This reads the label as 10 mg in 1 mL, a tenfold error.
whyNot.2: This uses a 20 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 100 mg in 1 mL on the label.

test.q: A service user is prescribed zuclopenthixol decanoate 200 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 500 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This uses a 200 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 500 mg in 1 mL on the label.
whyNot.3: This reads the label as 50 mg in 1 mL, a tenfold error.

test.q: A service user is prescribed haloperidol decanoate 175 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoules available each contain 50 mg in 1 mL. How many ampoules need to be opened?
test.why: 175 ÷ 50 = 3.5. A part ampoule cannot be opened, so round up to 4 ampoules.

whyNot.0: This rounds down: three ampoules hold 150 mg, less than the 175 mg prescribed.
whyNot.2: This is the exact quotient, but a part ampoule cannot be opened.
whyNot.3: This assumes 100 mg ampoules; the stock is 50 mg in 1 mL.

explain.body: 15 ÷ 20 = 0.75 exactly. If the stem asks for two decimal places, type 0.75 mL. Rounding to 0.8 mL loses a mark.

test.q: A service user is prescribed flupentixol decanoate 15 mg by deep intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 20 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.0: This rounds to one decimal place; the stem asks for two.
whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This uses a 100 mg in 1 mL strength, not the 20 mg in 1 mL on the label.
